limitations: Surface wetness layers are derived from C-band Sentinel-1 SAR backscatter, not direct root-zone soil moisture measurements.
High-risk alerts and rotation rankings are rule-based decision aids and require local verification of drainage feasibility, seed availability, soil pH, labor, and market demand.

rotation_strategies.name: Strategy 1: Nitrogen-Fixing & Soil Restorative Rotation
rotation_strategies.mechanics: Plant deep-rooted legumes during post-harvest bare-field windows identified from multi-year NDVI.
rotation_strategies.benefits: Restores soil organic matter, fixes atmospheric nitrogen (N2) to reduce synthetic fertilizer demand, and breaks root-knot nematode pest cycles.
rotation_strategies.risks_and_gaps: Requires local verification of mungbean/cowpea seed market availability and plot soil pH compatibility.

rotation_strategies.name: Strategy 2: Deep-Rooting & Erosion Control Cover Crop (Bio-Tillage)
rotation_strategies.mechanics: Seed deep-rooting cover crops across micro-slopes flagged by NASADEM as high-velocity runoff channels.
rotation_strategies.benefits: Creates sub-surface macro-pores that improve water infiltration, relieve surface ponding, and anchor topsoil against heavy rain erosion.
rotation_strategies.risks_and_gaps: Requires farmer and extension review of forage harvesting labor or machinery availability.

rotation_strategies.name: Strategy 3: Water-Conserving & Heat-Tolerant Short-Cycle Rotation
rotation_strategies.mechanics: Transition water-intensive crops during dry post-monsoon windows to short-cycle, low-water-demand grains.
rotation_strategies.benefits: Lowers seasonal irrigation demand during high-temperature windows while providing supplemental cash income.
rotation_strategies.risks_and_gaps: Local buyer demand and market price fluctuations require Municipal Agriculture Office / extension review.
